statement: A running model, not a calibrated one. The size and arrangement of the leaves, the length a shoot of the year makes before it flowers, the first-year cut and the pruning rule are from published descriptions of the cultivar, the hybrid or its parents; the weight and stiffness of a shoot in the air, node spacing, dates, how many shoots break and how many of them flower are choices tied to what those descriptions and photographs of the plant show; the routing and branching preferences of the framework are the Wisteria sinensis model's, kept for want of anything better. None has been measured on a plant. All its flowers are at the ends of side shoots of the year, as the plant's are. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: The truss ends a shoot of the year and carries on its line (Bean, of C. radicans: "in a cluster at the end of the current season's growth", https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/campsis/campsis-radicans/). It is a "lax truss" (Trees and Shrubs Online, of 'Mme Galen'), and in photographs of the cultivar (reference mg-ubc, mg-huntington) the shoot arches over under it, so that the truss hangs out and down from the end of an arching shoot; that comes from the shoot's mechanics, and the truss is held on the line of its shoot. That the pods hang is seen in photographs of the hybrid (reference hyb-fruit-1) and of C. radicans (rad-january-1).

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: Late into leaf: the University of Connecticut plant database says C. radicans is "late to leaf out in spring"; White Flower Farm's growing guide counts it among the last woody plants to leaf out (paraphrased: that page was not checked again). No source gives a date for Britain. Buds are taken to break on 12 April; the engine shows a leaf only once its shoot has grown past its first node, so the first leaves are out in the second week of May.

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: A shoot of the year stops lengthening when its truss forms at its tip ("New twigs grow about 60-80 cm before the flower buds appear", Havlis nursery catalogue); that is taken as 24 July, a few days before the first trusses open, and the framework is taken to stop with it. The engine stands a truss at the tip its shoot has reached on the day the truss opens, so a shoot must have stopped by then. No dated source.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: Not what times this plant's leaves: every leaf is on a shoot of the year and opens as that shoot is made. The window follows budburst for any leaf on older wood. No dated source.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: The leaves yellow a little before they drop: of C. radicans, "fall color is poor" and the foliage "yellow-green" (University of Connecticut), and "Leaves turn yellowish before dropping off in autumn" (Ohio State weed guide). Taken as mid October to early November; no dated source.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Leaves are taken to fall with the first frosts, from late October, and to be gone by late November. No dated source for Britain.

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: The truss forms at the tip of a shoot of the year once the shoot has made its length ("New twigs grow about 60-80 cm before the flower buds appear", Havlis nursery catalogue). The engine forms the buds of side shoots on the second day given here, 15 July, when the shoots have all but stopped; the first trusses then show as buds for two weeks before they open and the later ones for a month.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: The day a truss opens its first flower, 29 July to 2 October. RHS plant record: flowers in "late summer or early autumn"; RHS growing guide: "Flowers in late summer and autumn"; Bean, of C. radicans at Kew: flowers in August and September; Trees and Shrubs Online shows 'Mme Galen' in flower at Wisley and at Kew in July. With the days a truss lasts, the display runs to the end of October.

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: Not used while phenology.flowerLastsDays is set: each truss goes over its own number of days after it opens.

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: How long one truss is in flower, from its first trumpet opening to its last corolla dropping. A truss has six to twelve flowers that open a few at a time; a flower of C. radicans stops giving nectar 20 to 30 hours after it opens and its corolla stays on for several days (Bertin 1982, Amer. J. Bot. 69: 122-134, from the abstract). The number of days is a choice; nobody has timed a truss of this cultivar.

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: RHS growing guide: "Older plants can grow very large (up to 10m or 30ft high)"; RHS plant record: 8 to 12 m in 5 to 10 years, of a genus of "fast-growing deciduous climbers". Two metres of stem a season, with the slow start below, reaches the 10 m middle of that band in about six seasons. A size band is not a growth rate: a choice.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Branches of the framework, taken as slower than the main stems by steps. Not measured.

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: Not used while organs.whipShareOfNodes is 0. Kept for a scenario that switches long shoots on.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: A slow start: the RHS has every stem cut to 15 cm after planting and says the plant flowers once a woody framework has formed, in two to three years. The two factors are a choice.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: Three main stems from the base in the first season. RHS: after cutting back at planting, "train the strongest new shoots to fill the space" and remove the weaker; three is a choice.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: RHS campsis growing guide: after planting, cut all stems back to 15 cm from the ground.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Main stems, their branches and one more order make the framework; everything beyond is a shoot of the year. A choice.

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: The RHS ultimate-height band used as a cap on the length of a main stem. A height band is not a route length, so this is a stand-in.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Framework branches shorter than the main stems by halves. Not measured.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: The Wisteria sinensis model's value, kept: no source read says how this plant varies the length of its framework branches, and nothing in the photographs settles it. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: The Wisteria sinensis model's value, kept: no source read says how this plant branches its framework at a node of the support, and nothing in the photographs settles it. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: The Wisteria sinensis model's value, kept: no source read says how this plant leaves buds dormant, and nothing in the photographs settles it. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.budExtraDormancyYears.basis: The Wisteria sinensis model's value, kept: no source read says how this plant leaves buds dormant, and nothing in the photographs settles it. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: One framework stem to a lath or cable. The framework is kept spaced ("young growths should be carefully spaced and tied in", Trees and Shrubs Online; "train the strongest new shoots to fill the space", RHS), and its stems grow stout. A choice.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: The three main stems may go up one glulam member side by side before they part. A choice.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: The Wisteria sinensis model's value, kept: no source read says how this plant chooses its way at a node of the support; the gardener ties it in, and these numbers stand for where a trained stem goes, and nothing in the photographs settles it. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: Not used: the plant clings by aerial rootlets and does not pass round its support, so no grasp limit is asked for.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: Not applicable to this plant, which does not twine; present because every model carries every parameter.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: Not applicable to this plant, which does not twine; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: Stem between one pair of leaves and the next. No flora gives it; the University of Michigan climbers database says only that the internodes of C. radicans are long. Chosen so that a flowering shoot of 60 to 80 cm carries six to nine pairs of leaves below its truss.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: The whole pinnate leaf. Burras and Griffiths, Manual of Climbers and Wall Plants (1994), of the hybrid: "Leaves 20-35cm", as quoted by Discover Life (checked); Burncoose Nurseries gives this cultivar's leaves as up to 30 cm. Oates et al. (HortScience 49: 343-345, 2014) measured means of 262 to 396 mm on four other Campsis cultivars. The top of the range is drawn in a little because every leaf in a run is drawn from this one range.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: Leaves opposite: Missouri Plants gives the leaves of C. radicans as opposite and odd-pinnate; NC State Extension gives the hybrid's leaf arrangement as opposite. Every photograph of the cultivar looked at shows them in pairs (reference mg-stang-1, mg-vlasenko-a).

organs.spurChance.basis: No spurs are grown. The short wood of this plant is the stub a late-winter prune leaves of last year's flowering shoot, and the flowering side shoots below stand for what breaks from it.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: The length of a truss, from where it leaves the shoot to the mouths of its end flowers. Built from its parts: six to twelve flowers (Burncoose; RHS A-Z as cited by Wikipedia), each up to 8 cm long, on an axis that in the parent C. grandiflora is 15 to 20 cm (Flora of China, as reported by Wikipedia; the flora itself could not be opened). In photographs of the cultivar (reference mg-ubc, mg-huntington) a truss in flower is about a hand and a half long. No source measures a truss of this cultivar.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: No long non-flowering shoots are grown. The plant does make them (Bean, of C. radicans: even pruned every spring it keeps an "ungainly habit"), but the engine keeps a long shoot for ever unless a pruning routine cuts it, and none is modelled for this plant, so they would pile up year on year as bare sticks. The year's free growth is all in the flowering side shoots.

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: Deciduous: a leaf lasts the season it grew in.

organs.clearStemHeightM.basis: Shoots break down to the ground: C. radicans sprouts freely from its base (Oates et al. 2014, paraphrased; Missouri Plants: stems "multiple from base"). A gardener may keep the foot clear; none is modelled.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: RHS campsis growing guide: it flowers once a strong woody framework has formed, after about two to three years. Taken to flower first in its third season.

flowering.maturityRamp.basis: Few trusses in the first flowering year, more in the second, all the plant can carry from the third. A choice.

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant, which has no flowering spurs; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant, which is not summer pruned; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: None: the flowers are in a truss at the end of a shoot of the year, never at the leaf nodes along it (Bean, of C. radicans: "in a cluster at the end of the current season's growth"; Gentry 1992: a few-flowered terminal panicle). All flowering is at the ends of side shoots (sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare).

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant, which is not summer pruned; present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: RHS campsis growing guide: once a framework is established, "'spur-prune' the sideshoots annually in late winter", "cutting back all the sideshoots to within two or three buds of the main stems". No routine in the model makes this cut for this plant yet; the side shoots are shed after one season instead.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: A stem cut hard is taken to break from one or two buds below the cut (RHS renovation: cut to within 30 cm of the base and train the strongest new shoots). The count is a choice.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A young shoot about 5 mm through at its growing end. In a photograph of a node of the parent C. radicans (reference rad-rootlets) the one-year stem is about as thick as a pencil, some 6 mm; at the soft tip a little less. Not measured on this cultivar.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Chosen so that the main stem of a plant that has filled the specimen frame is about 5 cm through at the ground after ten years ("a stout main stem", Bean of C. radicans). Not measured.

thickening.branchShare.basis: The Wisteria sinensis model's value, kept: no source read says how this plant shares thickness between a stem and its branches, and nothing in the photographs settles it. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

fruit.setShare.basis: Share of trusses that leave a pod. Pods are rare in Britain: Bean, of C. radicans, says they form "Very rarely, but sometimes after unusually hot summers". The engine has no hot summers, so a small share is set every year: one truss in twenty-five. A choice.

fruit.lengthM.basis: From the parents: C. radicans "5 in. long, 3/4 in. wide in the middle" (Bean), C. grandiflora 7 to 12 cm (as reported by Wikipedia). The pods of the hybrid in photographs (reference hyb-fruit-1, October, Germany) are about as long as a hand. No source measures a pod of this cultivar.

fruit.swellDays.basis: Days from the last corolla dropping to a full-length green pod. A choice; not timed.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: The pod turns from green to tan and dries from mid October to mid December (University of Connecticut, of C. radicans: the capsules "change from green to tan"; reference hyb-fruit-1 shows the hybrid's pods still grey-green on 25 October). Dates are a choice.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: A window early in the year, so the dry pods hang through winter (USDA NRCS plant guide, of C. radicans: the fruit may be thought decorative in winter; reference rad-january-1 shows split tan pods on the old truss in January) and are gone before the plant comes into leaf. Dates are a choice.

appendages.tendrilNodePattern.basis: No tendrils: the plant holds on by aerial rootlets alone (RHS growing guide: "using aerial roots along its long stems to grip onto vertical surfaces").

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: The leaf stalks do not coil: the plant holds on by rootlets alone (RHS growing guide, as for appendages.tendrilNodePattern).

appendages.aerialRootPatchSpacingM.basis: Stem between one tuft of rootlets and the next. In C. radicans they form in two rows in bands below the stem nodes (Ohio State weed guide), which would be a tuft at every node; C. grandiflora has few or none (Burras and Griffiths), and this hybrid clings weakly (Trees and Shrubs Online: "It is not a climber that can be left to look after itself"), so fewer than one a node are drawn. A choice.

appendages.aerialRootLengthM.basis: Length of one rootlet. No source measures them. In a photograph of the parent C. radicans (reference rad-rootlets) a tuft beside a node reaches out about one and a half times the width of a stem some 6 mm through, so 5 to 10 mm is taken.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Unarmed: no flora or photograph read shows prickles or thorns on Campsis.

sideShoots.bearingWoodAgeYears.basis: The shoots of the year break from wood made in an earlier year: from the two or three buds a late-winter prune leaves at the base of last year's shoot (RHS).

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: Shoots of the year for each metre of framework. With a pair of buds at every node, about 0.095 m apart, a metre has some twenty buds, and a spur cut to two or three buds (RHS: "cutting back all the sideshoots to within two or three buds of the main stems") breaks more than one; about one bud in three is taken to make a shoot. Set so that a plant of six years clothes the specimen frame in summer, which is well inside the 2.5 to 4 m spread the RHS gives it at five to ten years. A choice; nobody has counted.

sideShoots.lengthM.basis: Havlis nursery catalogue, of this cultivar: "New twigs grow about 60-80 cm before the flower buds appear" (checked 13 November 2026).

sideShoots.lifespanYears.basis: Left uncut, a shoot of the year stays on the plant as its own wood (the RHS spur-prunes the side shoots because they would otherwise stay: "Plants can be pruned annually to keep them within bounds"). No source read says how long such a shoot lives; 30 seasons is longer than any run here, so nothing is shed in a run. On the gardened plant the late-winter spur prune (trumpetVineRoutine, RHS: "cutting back all the sideshoots to within two or three buds of the main stems") takes the year's shoots back to stubs, and next year's shoots break from the stubs. Until 13 November 2026 this was 1, a stand-in for that cut.

sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare.basis: Share of the year's shoots that end in a truss on a plant in sun in a warm place. RHS growing guide: "It flowers best in full sun, in a warm sheltered spot" and "low temperatures or dry soil can cause flower buds to be shed"; Havlis: in partial shade "the flowers will be fewer and their colour less intense". The share is a choice; in a cool summer it would be less.

sideShoots.baseDiameterMm.basis: A shoot of the year 80 cm long taken as about 6 mm through at its foot, tapering to the 5 mm of its soft tip. In a photograph of a node of the parent C. radicans (reference rad-rootlets) a stem of one year is about 6 mm through; nothing measures a shoot of this cultivar.

mechanics.greenShootModulusMPa.basis: The soft growing end, taken at half the generic 300 MPa and below the least stiff searcher base Hattermann et al. 2022 measured (213 MN/m2, https://doi.org/10.3389/ffgc.2022.836247), since a growing tip is softer than a base: the shoot is pithy and its wood fragile (Havlis: "Trumpet creeper has fragile wood which, if too long, can easily become a target for strong wind or heavy snowfall"), and in photographs its leafy ends arch over (reference mg-ubc). Not measured.

mechanics.woodSetDays.basis: The year's shoot stays green and soft for two months behind its tip. The RHS asks for full sun "in order to ripen the wood so it flowers freely", that is, the wood of the year ripens late in the season; the generic month is lengthened to two. Not measured.

mechanics.woodModulusMPa.basis: Set wood of the year, taken below the generic 3000 MPa for a wood the nursery calls "fragile" (Havlis) and whose shoots in photographs arch over under their leaves and a truss (reference mg-ubc) rather than stand. Hattermann et al. 2022 found about 3000 MN/m2 needed for a searcher to span more than about 0.8 m; a shoot of this plant spans less before it bends. Not measured.

mechanics.leafFreshMassPerAreaKgM2.basis: Worked out, not weighed. A leaf of 26 cm has nine leaflets of about 6 by 3 cm (morphology.json), some 105 cm2 of blade; at about 0.22 kg of fresh leaf to the square metre, ordinary for a thin deciduous leaf, and with its stalk and axis, about 3.3 g. The engine takes the outline of a leaf as a disc 0.56 of its length across, 167 cm2 for that leaf, so 3.3 g over it is 0.2 kg/m2.

mechanics.inflorescenceFreshMassKg.basis: Worked out, not weighed. A corolla of this plant is thick and leathery (Missouri Plants calls that of C. radicans thickened), some 70 cm2 of tube and limb about 0.6 mm thick, about 4 g; a truss has six to twelve flowers (Burncoose), of which a few are open at a time and the rest calyces and buds (reference mg-huntington), with its axis: about 30 g.

mechanics.fruitFreshMassKg.basis: Worked out, not weighed. A spindle-shaped pod about 10 cm long and 2 cm through (Bean, of C. radicans) holds about 15 cm3; green and full of seed, about 15 g.

mechanics.searcherReachM.basis: The farthest a shoot of the year holds itself out before it arches over. Hattermann et al. 2022 (https://doi.org/10.3389/ffgc.2022.836247) give 0.14 to 0.91 m for tendril and root climbers together; in photographs of the cultivar (reference mg-ubc, mg-huntington) the leafy shoots that carry trusses arch over and hang within about half a metre of where they leave the plant. A reading from photographs; not measured.

attachment.graspReachM.basis: A shoot in the air takes hold again only where it comes to lie on a surface: the plant holds by rootlets a centimetre or less long (reference rad-rootlets) and its shoots do not revolve or twine round a support. Two centimetres is a choice.

organs.leafTurnToOpenShare.basis: On a wall the leaves turn out from it and hang face out, the end leaflet lowest, whichever way the stem runs (reference hyb-badduben-1, a planting of the hybrid on a house wall). More than the generic half way; a reading from a photograph.

sideShoots.branchAngleDeg.basis: Shoots of the year leave the framework at wide angles, many nearly square to it (reference mg-stang-2, hyb-badduben-1, mg-helbra-1). Read from photographs; not measured.

sideShoots.breakSpreadDays.basis: The plant is late into leaf and its buds break over several weeks from late April into May (University of Connecticut: "Late to leaf out in spring", of C. radicans). Six weeks from a week after bud burst is a choice.

tropism.turnPerM.basis: How sharply a growing shoot turns up and towards the light. A shoot of this plant neither twines nor searches upright: it grows out from the wall and its end hangs (reference mg-ubc, hyb-badduben-1). Taken weaker than the generic 1.5 rad/m. A choice, not measured.

mechanics.stemFreshDensityKgM3.basis: A fresh shoot is mostly water: 1000 kg/m3, the figure Chelakkot and Mahadevan 2017 take for a young shoot (https://doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2017.0001), the same as the generic. Not weighed for this plant.

organs.alternateDivergenceDeg.basis: Not used: the leaves stand in opposite pairs, each pair a right angle round the stem from the last (decussate), which the engine does without this number. Given so that a run does not report a generic value for a plant with no single leaves.
